html:
Quito is the capital of Ecuador, high in the Andes just south of the equator. The Spanish founded their city on 6 December 1534 on the site of an Inca town burned by the general Rumiñahui as he retreated.

Quito had been the northern capital of the Inca Empire under Huayna Capac. Under Spain it became the seat of a royal court, the Audiencia of Quito, and a city of convents and churches, filled with the painting and carving of the Quito School.

It led the first rising for self-rule in 1809 and won freedom at the Battle of Pichincha in 1822. Its old centre, among the best-preserved in Latin America, was among the first places named World Heritage Sites in 1978. Quito and Guayaquil have been rivals in Ecuador ever since.
